item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Not only does this thing resemble the soul-extractor, but there's also a red quartz SCP (I don't remember the number) that does more or less the exact same thing as this needle. Maybe that article's newer than this one, but they're so incredibly similar, I'm not too okay with both of them existing…and I feel like that one does it a bit better than this one does (no offense, but it's quartz that records memories and such, for anyone to later see [whether they want to or not]).

Maybe I'm missing something that sets them far apart, but the thing what removes your memories and gives them to someone else exists elsewhere, and in a better form; and while I generally try to judge each SCP individually, as though I never read any others before, I just can't really like this one. I agree with previous people that having no negative side effects would kind of make it too…lame, I guess, but maybe just keep the way the recipients go crazy so easily - even expand on that aspect - and take out the "it removes the donors' memories" bit. Besides, not all SCP's have to be things what do horrible things to people - they just have to be impossible and, at minimum, a bit creepy. That's just my opinion, though. :)

Hmm, I don't know. We already have a Soul Extractor with serious consequences for the donor; I don't really see that this article would be improved by making it hurt the donor directly.

Perhaps you could address the indirect harm — namely, violation of privacy. What if the object imparted precise knowledge to the donor of what had been transferred? Knowing exactly which of my private thoughts had just been drawn out of me and handed to someone else would make me positively sick with revulsion.
